No — this sentence has two problems and shouldn't go out as-is.

**1. "Fully compliant with the framework" is a compliance claim, not a lineage claim.**
NIST SP 800-61 is a public guideline (verified-public, easy to link — https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r2/final), so *citing* it is fine. But "fully compliant" implies you've been assessed against or formally meet the framework's requirements. Unless you've actually gone through some kind of audit/assessment against SP 800-61, this is an overstated-lineage claim — it reads as compliance/certification rather than "we drew on this."

**2. The uncited SRE talk is a "public-url-needed" source, not a citable one.**
"We don't have a link or citation for it handy" is the exact rationalization to watch for — if you can't verify or link it, it can't be published as a named source. Either find the talk (speaker, conference, year, link) or drop the specific attribution.

Suggested rewrite:

> "Our workflow draws on [NIST SP 800-61, the Computer Security Incident Handling Guide](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r2/final), and was also shaped by general SRE incident-response practices we've encountered at industry conferences. This toolkit is not certified or formally assessed against SP 800-61."

Or if you can track down the SRE talk, name it properly (speaker/conference/year/link) instead of leaving it uncited.

Want me to help track down the SRE talk citation or find a specific spot in your docs to drop this in?
